## Findings ledger
- [D3.DOC5.F2] Riley reads Weber’s political capitalism as linking imperialism to higher-return investments, arms production and state loans, and therefore as supporting a material prognosis of imperialist expansion — dim: theme_position — anchor: "Imperialist adventures, investments in arms manufacture, and state loans (phenomena that Weber grouped under the term political capitalism) tended in contrast to have higher rates of return" — doc: em:PSYPHAPS — reader: Dylan Riley — theme-origin: plan_spine — theme: Political capitalism, imperialism and tax-farming — plan-theme-link: Political capitalism, imperialism and tax-farming — position: Riley presents Weber’s account as materially close to the Lenin/Hobson thesis: declining returns in ordinary investment encourage political-capitalist expansion under interstate competition — confidence: high — trimmed-anchor: yes

scope_outcomes.criterion: The citing author must address at least one supplied engagement theme or introduce a clearly supported additional theme in the supplied text.
scope_outcomes.basis: The article explicitly discusses Weber’s account of imperialism, political capitalism, prestige and status, Marxian explanations, historical totalization, and the conditions of social citizenship.
limitations: The finding concerns this 2013 article only, not Riley’s complete work.
Tax-farming and a sustained treatment of patrimonialism or bureaucracy are not established in the inspected text.
